summary: Defines IS-IS extensions that let a Path Computation Client automatically find Path Computation Elements and learn their capabilities. It parallels the OSPF extensions in RFC 5088. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5089 lets IS-IS advertise which routers or servers can calculate network paths. The announcement identifies each service and the kinds of paths it can handle.

questions: how to discover pce with is-is
what is a path computation element
subtitle: How IS-IS advertises path-computation services and the path scopes they support.

tldr.problem: A Path Computation Client needs to discover Path Computation Elements and learn what kinds of paths each one can compute.
tldr.mechanism: A PCE Discovery sub-TLV is carried in the IS-IS Router Capability TLV. Its fields identify the PCE, its supported path scopes, domains, preferences, and capabilities.
tldr.outcome: IS-IS flooding lets clients learn about PCE changes and failures within the routing domain. The RFC is updated by RFC 9353.

today: RFC 5089 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2008 and is updated by RFC 9353.

sections.title: Finding Path Computation Elements
sections.content:
A Path Computation Client (PCC) asks a Path Computation Element (PCE) to calculate a network path. A network can have multiple PCEs with different capabilities, so a client needs a way to discover them and detect changes or failures.

RFC 5089 defines PCE discovery through IS-IS advertisements. It carries a PCE Discovery (PCED) sub-TLV inside the IS-IS Router Capability TLV. The RFC leaves the client's selection algorithm and discovery across autonomous-system boundaries outside its scope.
sections.plainLanguage: IS-IS can announce which PCEs are available in a routing domain. This RFC defines the information a PCE places in that announcement.

sections.title: Information and Flooding Scope
sections.content:
A PCE announcement can include the PCE's IPv4 or IPv6 address, supported path scopes, domains visible to the PCE, neighboring domains it can compute toward, and capability flags. Path scopes include intra-area, inter-area, inter-AS, and inter-layer computation.

IS-IS can flood the information within one Level 1 area, through an area and its Level 2 sub-domain, or across the entire IS-IS routing domain. The information is expected to change mainly when the PCE is configured, activated, deactivated, or fails.
sections.plainLanguage: The announcement says where a PCE can be reached and what it can compute. IS-IS controls how widely that information is shared.

sections.title: The PCED Sub-TLV
sections.content:
The PCED sub-TLV has type 5 and contains an unordered set of sub-TLVs. Its format uses a one-octet type, one-octet length, and a value. It is carried inside the IS-IS Router Capability TLV.

PCE-ADDRESS and PATH-SCOPE are required. PCE-DOMAIN, NEIG-PCE-DOMAIN, and PCE-CAP-FLAGS are optional. A receiver must silently ignore any unrecognized sub-TLV. The PCE address may appear for IPv4 and IPv6, but not more than once for either address type.
sections.plainLanguage: The PCED sub-TLV is a compact container inside an IS-IS capability announcement. It always includes the PCE address and supported path scope.

sections.title: Path Scopes and Preferences
sections.content:
The PATH-SCOPE sub-TLV indicates which path computations the PCE supports. Flags identify intra-area, inter-area, inter-AS, and inter-layer paths, plus default-PCE roles. Four three-bit preference fields rank the PCE for each scope, with 7 as the highest preference.

Operators can use preference values to influence how requests are distributed among PCEs. The actual selection and load-balancing policy is left to the PCC or network.
sections.plainLanguage: The scope flags list the types of paths a PCE can calculate. Preference values let local policy rank PCEs for those tasks.

sections.title: Updating Advertisements and Protecting Them
sections.content:
The IS-IS speaker must update its LSP when the PCE is activated, deactivated, or changes parameters. An advertisement is current only while the router that sent it remains reachable. A change to PCED information must not trigger an SPF computation at receiving routers.

Routers that do not support the PCED sub-TLV silently ignore it. Discovery relies on IS-IS security; IS-IS mechanisms can protect LSP authenticity and integrity, but do not encrypt the discovery information. RFC 5089 is updated by RFC 9353.
sections.plainLanguage: IS-IS announcements must change when a PCE changes or becomes unavailable. Authentication can protect the announcement from tampering, but not from being read.

items.label: PCE-ADDRESS
items.desc: Address used to reach the PCE.

items.label: PCE-DOMAIN
items.desc: Domain where the PCE has visibility.

items.label: NEIG-PCE-DOMAIN
items.desc: Neighbor domain toward which the PCE can compute.
